title: Understanding the Null Hypothesis
text: The null hypothesis states that the proportion of adults in Berkeley that consume at least $$1$$ soda every day is 72%. This means we assume $$p=0.72$$ unless proven otherwise.

title: Significance Level and Rejection
text: A 5% significance level means that we are willing to accept a 5% chance of incorrectly rejecting the null hypothesis. If the null hypothesis is rejected, it suggests that the true proportion is significantly different from 72%.

title: Sample Proportion and Decision
text: The sample proportion, denoted as \( \hat{\alpha} \), is $$0.67$$. Compare this with the hypothesized proportion of $$0.72$$ to determine if the null hypothesis should be rejected.

title: Calculating the Test Statistic
text: To determine if the null hypothesis should be rejected, calculate the test statistic using the formula: \( z=(\hat{\alpha}-p)/(sqrt(p*(1-p)/n)) \), where \( $$\hat{\alpha}=0.67$$ \), \( $$p=0.72$$ \), and \( $$n=1000$$ \).

title: Interpreting the Test Statistic
text: Once you have calculated the test statistic, compare it to the critical value for a 5% significance level. If the test statistic falls outside the critical value range, the null hypothesis is rejected.

title: Conclusion Based on the Test
text: If the test statistic indicates rejection of the null hypothesis, it means the sample provides sufficient evidence to conclude that the true proportion of adults in Berkeley consuming at least $$1$$ soda every day is not 72%.
